how: Calls ask members to bring Lord Eder onto the canvas and help others experience their Lord.
The proposer names the mark and its location before another participant reports completion, without establishing leadership or who placed first.
Proposals identify the figure and later suggest signing its logo to make the subreddit recognisable.
Collective success and presence are reported in the thread, while the allocation of actual pixel work remains unseen.
An anchor coordinate locates the proposed figure, and a later post circulates a plan attributed to another room.
A one-line collective completion answer accepts the proposal without asking anything back or identifying the author's individual pixel labour.
Brief success claims, praise and retrospective celebration mark the achieved image as a collective accomplishment.
Public thanks credit another room for collaborating on and tolerating the shrine.
An ending announcement and its answer record closure, including a participant learning about it late because of work.
Thanks establish reported collaboration and tolerance without demonstrating a reciprocal bargain or negotiated border.
Attributing a new plan to another room makes a specific contribution visible without showing its production or adoption.
The candidate explains recruiting for the canvas through the room's familiar devotion to Lord Eder.
Warnings about children and blasphemy continue the separate fake-Eder joke as ordinary room talk.
The fake-Eder thread predates the event, so its surviving replies cannot establish April Fools licence as the source of its joking.
Location proposals and success claims do not report a shortage of hands, overcrowding or a judgment that the room was outclassed.
Proposals and an externally attributed plan cannot determine whether leadership, votes or work divisions were decided beyond the visible thread.
Success and collaboration are reported without describing watching, repair or defence, leaving upkeep unseen rather than unnecessary.
The broad claim that bots took over does not trace particular changes to the shrine or identify responsible placers.
Thanks for tolerance do not show members refusing damage, restraining attackers, apologising or repairing a neighbour's work.
The credited collaboration supplies no border, truce or bargain whose terms can be read.
The surviving recruitment call seeks the Lord's presence without directing an attack on another work.
A new plan is shared without identifying a lost spot, a decision to abandon it or a relocation.
Retrospective celebration and thanks do not show a successor canvas, reused emblem or decision to preserve ties.
The claim that bots took over names no operators or machine placement by this room.
Reported collaboration does not establish a coalition, shared governing chat or mutual-defence agreement.
The credited collaborator and general remark about bots do not identify a rival-directed contest in this room's talk.
A proposed spot under a flag and thanks for tolerance do not establish occupation of host territory under the host's rules.
The call and its completion answer show no boundary-setting around canvas talk, without proving that moderation was unnecessary.
The tentative authority dispute is not visible in the thanks for collaboration or the attributed plan.
The tentative dispute over preserved versions is not visible in retrospective praise and thanks.
Devotional recruitment names no pre-existing quarrel or rival carried into the canvas.
The call uses devotion to recruit help without naming an enemy or invoking an earlier rivalry to justify attack.
Sharing an externally credited plan does not establish that its poster represented the room in negotiations.
The proposal receives an explicit completion claim, supporting the reported response sequence while leaving recruitment's effect on actual placement unobserved.
The later call does not recall the earlier proposer, so their order does not establish that the starter generated the call.
A completion claim has no cited upkeep response, so the proposed building-to-maintenance mechanism cannot be tested.
Reported collaboration contains no account of upkeep bringing the room into border negotiations.
Thanks for tolerance supply neither an agreed border nor a restraint response caused by that border.
An unattributed ending claim about bots cannot test whether upkeep pressure drove this room to automate.
The same brief turn reports completion and celebrates, so it cannot establish a separate reporting-then-celebrating causal step.
Celebration precedes end-marking without a cited turn linking celebration to an intention to preserve a record.
End-marking and later thanks show no decision to carry an image, organisation or relationship into a continuing effort.
The new plan identifies neither insufficient hands nor a move caused by that assessment.
Coordinates accompany the opening proposal, and the later externally attributed plan does not demonstrate design argument being settled by an agreed template.
The proposal receives a bare completion answer, while silent acceptance and the preference for reasoned refusals cannot be tested here.
The attributed plan and collaborative thanks do not describe upkeep strain causing a request for other rooms' help.
Crediting collaboration does not establish prior border negotiations or a bargain that opened a channel for help.
The recruitment call names the desired figure without showing the room turning its recruited hands against a rival.
The surviving call and thanks identify no attack-refusal pair from which to test the restraint mechanism.
The visible collaboration is not linked to an attack call answered by a truce or alternative bargain.
The recruitment call does not identify an attack that generated subsequent rival-directed talk.
Thanks for collaboration do not establish defensive pressure leading the room into a coalition.
A canvas call is visible without an account of a resulting flood or host response that draws a posting boundary.
The tentative agreement-to-authority-dispute mechanism cannot be tested from a plan attribution and thanks without an agreement or representation dispute.
Marking the end includes informing a participant who remained unaware because of work, making closure something learned through an exchange rather than knowledge already shared.
Signing the canvas mark is proposed to bring people into the subreddit, so the local explanation must preserve intended growth without claiming that newcomers actually arrived.
